title: Per-unit eval score
description: The reconciling verifier writes one of these per unit. These are AGENT-WEAKNESS metrics under the dual-input probe: the implementer was given BOTH the spec AND the business requirement, so a miss is an agent weakness, not a spec-completeness gap. Code quality is graded vs the human diff as a REFERENCE (better/equal/worse), NEVER as a match target — there is deliberately no 'human-match %'. Consumed by core/lib/aggregate_scores.py and core/lib/build_report.py.

id.description: Unit key — a ticket key, PR number, or tagged commit, e.g. BILL-1234

compile.description: Real build/type-check verdict grepped from the log (never the wrapper exit code), or n/a for a repo with no build_cmd and no typecheck_cmd.

business_req_pct.description: Weighted % of the atomic acceptance criteria achieved, graded against the REAL business ask (not spec-line coverage). Headline number. aggregate_scores.py RECOMPUTES it from business_criteria when they are present (full=1, partial=0.5, none=0, weight-normalised) and uses the recomputed value; invalid criteria make it null ('not measured') in scores.json, never 0.

business_req_source.description: Set by aggregate_scores.py (score_hygiene.recompute), not by the grader: where business_req_pct came from.

business_req_pct_reported.description: Set by aggregate_scores.py when the grader's own business_req_pct disagreed with the value recomputed from business_criteria (the recomputed value wins).

business_criteria.description: The business requirement + spec decomposed into weighted atomic criteria, each graded with file:line evidence.

weight.description: Relative weight; the pct is the weighted roll-up.

code_quality.description: Each axis is better|equal|worse vs the human REFERENCE — a different-but-equal-or-better solution is not a defect. Do NOT emit a match-percentage.

security.description: Only net-new REACHABLE threat vs the human diff baseline. A theoretical/unreachable issue is not a finding.

hallucination.description: 'none' or a description of an invented symbol/API (the compile-gate is the concrete detector).

overeng.description: 'none' or scope built that the ask did not need.

lost_context.description: 'none' or: locally-correct output the consumer never reads, or a value the producer never emits. The signature weakness this eval exists to catch.

caught_spec_error.description: Positive signal: the agent flagged a spec/business-req problem instead of blindly following it.

divergence.description: How the AI approach differs from the human reference (neutral).

verdict.description: The reconciled one-line verdict shown on the scoreboard.

documented_only.description: true = attempted but not scored (e.g. infra-stalled, or an anti-over-engineering no-op); rendered in a separate 'documented, not scored' section.

arm.description: Which ablation arm produced this score. ABSENT defaults to 'harness' (back-compat). ANY string is a distinct arm (N-arm): the canonical ones are 'harness' (the sandbox staged with the project's full skills — mapping + GUARD + …) and 'baseline' (the SAME fork-point / SPEC / business requirement with skills stripped to EMPTY and no GUARD pack); a run may add further arms, e.g. 'mapping+oracle' via score.mapping+oracle.json. aggregate_scores.py globs <UNIT>/score*.json, groups by this raw field into aggregate.arms, and emits ablation_delta (harness − baseline) plus arm_deltas (each non-baseline arm vs baseline).

scorer_model.description: The scorer's model id (e.g. the reconciling verifier's model).

scorer_family.description: The scorer's model family (e.g. claude, gemini, gpt, glm). aggregate_scores.py flags SAME-FAMILY SCORING when it matches implementer_family or improver_family (self-preference risk).

improver_family.description: For a retest: the model family that proposed the skill edits being measured.

blind_label.description: Set by score_hygiene.py unblind: the opaque label (A, B, …) this arm was scored under; the scorer never saw the arm name.

scorer.description: Who produced this score. 'adversarial-review-loop' = the reviewer → red-team → reconciling-verifier protocol; 'stub' = fixture constants (tests/demos — not a measurement); any other string is shown as written. ABSENT is reported as an unrecorded scorer. aggregate_scores.py builds the report headline's provenance from this field and prefixes 'STUB RUN' whenever any score is a stub.

oracle.description: OPTIONAL behavioural-oracle grounding for this unit: a single mined oracle that was witnessed or run for it. A FLOOR — witnessed literal + its site only; NEVER an inferred 'what the test proves'. Emitted by core/lib/oracle_scan.py, promoted to tier RUN by the verify adapter when the oracle actually executed. All fields optional; back-compatible.

tier.description: Strength-of-evidence tier: RUN = executed and passed just now; WITNESSED = a concrete expected literal read at a file:line (asserted, not run here); STUB = a test with no real assertion (counted, never grounding); UNVERIFIED = referenced but no oracle found.

expected.description: The asserted literal/behaviour, or '—' for a stub.

cutoff_label.description: Pretraining-cutoff label, computed by core/lib/cutoff_label.py from the unit's merged_at + the project's decontamination.cutoff_policy (repo_visibility / model_cutoff). 'cutoff-clean' = the unit could NOT be in public pretraining (private repo, or merged after the model cutoff); 'cutoff-unverified' = it might be. A HEADLINE number must come from cutoff-clean units.

cutoff_reason.description: Human-readable justification for cutoff_label, e.g. 'private repo — not in public pretraining' or 'merged 2025-06-01 after model cutoff 2025-01-01'.

decontam_confidence.description: How thoroughly this unit was decontaminated: 'auto+curated' = the automated leak gate AND a curated answer-token list both ran; 'auto-only' = only the automated gate; 'curated-only' = only a curated token list; 'nothing-checked' = neither; 'hand-mitigated' = a known overlap was manually mitigated. Surfaced as a per-unit chip in the report.

artifacts.description: Relative-to-unit-dir (or absolute) paths to the on-disk evidence.
